title: 2 Kings 10
paragraphs: ¹ Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria — to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and the guardians of Ahab's children. He said, ² "As soon as this letter reaches you — you have your master's sons with you, and you have chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons — ³ choose the best and most capable of your master's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house." ⁴ But they were terrified and said, "If two kings could not stand against him, how can we?" ⁵ So the palace administrator, the city governor, the elders, and the guardians all sent this message to Jehu: "We are your servants and will do whatever you say. We will not make anyone king. Do whatever you think is best."

⁶ Then Jehu wrote them a second letter: "If you are on my side and will obey me, bring the heads of your master's sons to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." The king's sons, seventy of them, were being raised by the city's leading men. ⁷ When the letter arrived, they took the king's sons and killed all seventy of them, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel. ⁸ A messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." He said, "Stack them in two piles at the entrance of the gate until morning." ⁹ In the morning Jehu went out and stood before all the people and said, "You are innocent. It was I who conspired against my master and killed him. But who killed all of these? ¹⁰ Know then that not a word the LORD has spoken against the house of Ahab will fail. The LORD has done what he promised through his servant Elijah."

¹¹ Then Jehu killed everyone remaining in Jezreel who belonged to the house of Ahab — all his chief men, his close friends, and his priests — leaving him no survivor. ¹² He set out and left for Samaria. Along the way, at Beth Eked of the Shepherds, ¹³ Jehu came across the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and asked, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are relatives of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother." ¹⁴ "Take them alive," he said. They took them alive and slaughtered them by the well at Beth Eked — forty-two men. He left not one of them alive. ¹⁵ After leaving there, he found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him and asked, "Are you of one mind with me, as I am with you?" "I am," Jehonadab answered. "If you are," said Jehu, "give me your hand." So Jehonadab gave him his hand, and Jehu pulled him up into the chariot.

¹⁶ Jehu said, "Come with me and see how devoted I am to the LORD." And they had him ride with him in the chariot. ¹⁷ When Jehu arrived in Samaria, he killed everyone there who remained from Ahab's family until he had destroyed it completely, just as the LORD had said to Elijah. ¹⁸ Then Jehu called all the people together and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much. ¹⁹ Now summon all the prophets of Baal, all his ministers, and all his priests. See that no one is missing, because I am going to hold a great sacrifice for Baal. Anyone who fails to come will not live." But this was a trap Jehu had set in order to kill the worshippers of Baal. ²⁰ Jehu said, "Call an assembly in honor of Baal." So they proclaimed it.

²¹ Jehu sent word throughout all Israel, and every single worshipper of Baal came — not one stayed away. They crowded into the temple of Baal until it was packed from one end to the other. ²² Jehu told the keeper of the wardrobe, "Bring out garments for all the worshippers of Baal." The garments were brought out. ²³ Then Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab went into the temple of Baal. Jehu said to the worshippers of Baal, "Search carefully and make sure there are no servants of the LORD here with you — only worshippers of Baal." ²⁴ They went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and said, "If any of you lets a single man escape — anyone I am placing in your hands — you will pay for his life with your own." ²⁵ As soon as Jehu had finished offering the burnt offering, he ordered the guards and officers, "Go in and kill them — let no one escape." They cut them down with the sword, and the guards and officers threw the bodies out and went into the inner shrine of the temple of Baal.

²⁶ They brought out the sacred stone from the temple of Baal and burned it. ²⁷ They demolished the sacred stone of Baal and tore down the temple of Baal, turning it into a latrine — as it remains to this day. ²⁸ In this way Jehu wiped out the worship of Baal from Israel. ²⁹ But he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin — the worship of the golden calves at Bethel and Dan. ³⁰ The LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my eyes and have treated the house of Ahab just as I intended, your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel."

³¹ Yet Jehu was not careful to keep the law of the LORD God of Israel wholeheartedly. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who had caused Israel to sin. ³² In those days the LORD began to reduce the size of Israel. Hazael defeated the Israelites throughout their territory — ³³ east of the Jordan, all the land of Gilead: the territories of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh, from Aroer by the Arnon Gorge through Gilead and Bashan. ³⁴ As for the other events of Jehu's reign, everything he did and all his achievements, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel? ³⁵ Jehu rested with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz succeeded him as king.
³⁶ Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.
